title: Rast wins Zolder Race 2 as Eng takes the points lead
dek: René Rast won Race 2 at Zolder for Audi Sport Team Rosberg by 9.845 seconds from Philipp Eng, who took the championship lead after a safety car and a late fight for third.

chapters.title: A safety car reshapes the standings
text: Saturday’s opener had turned on a safety car. Philipp Eng won from seventh on the grid for BMW Team RMR, with Joel Eriksson second and Nico Müller third, after the leaders Bruno Spengler, Marco Wittmann and René Rast were caught before their mandatory stops. Wittmann, who started from pole, finished seventh but kept the championship lead on 43 points, ahead of Eng on 40 and Müller on 37.

Rast had dropped out of the race with a technical problem. At Hockenheim he had followed a difficult Saturday with a Sunday win from 16th on the grid, so Zolder offered him a second chance to recover on the second day.

chapters.title: Van der Linde takes pole by 0.006 seconds
text: Sheldon van der Linde took the first DTM pole of his career for BMW Team RBM, his 1:21.590 beating Rast’s 1:21.596 by just 0.006 seconds. The rookie had run into the gravel at Turn 4 straight after setting his time, but kept enough momentum to rejoin and stayed on top when the session ended.

Eng qualified third on 1:21.714, ahead of Robin Frijns and Timo Glock. Mike Rockenfeller was sixth after the clutch problem that left him 16th on Saturday, with Wittmann seventh, Jonathan Aberdein eighth, Jamie Green ninth and Eriksson tenth. Jake Dennis led R-Motorsport in 13th, ahead of Pietro Fittipaldi and Spengler, who was 15th.

The session was stopped by a red flag in the closing minutes when Paul di Resta stopped his Aston Martin on track, and he did not start the race from 18th. Ferdinand Habsburg lined up 17th and Daniel Juncadella 16th.

chapters.title: Rast passes the pole-sitter on lap 11
text: Rast made a poor start and van der Linde kept the lead. Eng, attacking in the opening laps, made a mistake and dropped from third to fifth, which left Rast free to chase the leader. Rast spent the first stint alternately backing off and pushing to look after his tyres, since wear was seen as the key to passing at Zolder.

He finally got by at Turn 1 on lap 11, and van der Linde pitted at the end of that lap. Eng had stopped early, gained a place on Glock with the undercut and passed Frijns on track with a move down the hill. Rast came out of the stops ahead of the others but had to defend hard on cold tyres.

chapters.title: Wittmann hits Frijns and the safety car comes out
text: Once the stops were done, Wittmann hit the rear-left of Frijns’s Audi in the fight for fifth and spun him off. Frijns said afterwards that his Audi had lost power at that moment. The recovery of the Audi brought out the safety car for five laps, and the race was extended by five minutes plus one lap to make up the time.

Wittmann was penalised for the contact. At the IndyCar-style restart he and Glock ran onto the grass and lost ground, and Wittmann eventually finished 13th. Rast held his lead through the restart despite a minor error at the Villeneuve chicane, and Eng slid past van der Linde to take second.

chapters.title: Rast wins by 9.845 seconds as Green steals third
text: Rast pulled clear after the restart and won by 9.845 seconds from Eng, who also set the fastest lap. The fight for the last place on the podium went to the final lap. Green, on a two-stop strategy and fresh tyres, had come through the pack, and he passed van der Linde for third at Turn 4. Rockenfeller dived down the inside, ran across the grass in the process and failed to take third, but he did take fourth from van der Linde, who finished fifth.

Dennis was sixth, the best result of the season so far for R-Motorsport. He had passed Glock, who stopped one lap from the end and was classified 14th, a lap down. Spengler, Müller, Fittipaldi and Eriksson completed the top ten, with Duval 11th, Aberdein 12th and Wittmann 13th. Juncadella and Habsburg retired with technical problems, Frijns was out after the contact, and di Resta did not start.

chapters.title: Eng leads the championship, Wittmann loses ground
text: Rast called his Audi fantastic and said he would like to win on a Saturday for a change, rather than only on Sundays. He said that the points lost in the retirement on Saturday had been valuable, as they had been at Hockenheim, and that it was good to have held contact with the leaders over the weekend.

Eng left Belgium leading the championship after a win and a second place. He said he could get used to the lead. He also said that he had been too ambitious on the opening lap, trying to go around van der Linde on the outside, locking a wheel and letting three cars through, and that a better start could have given him more.

Wittmann went into the weekend as championship leader and left without points on Sunday, a day after the safety car had cost him the chance of a win. He accepted the penalty and apologised to Frijns, who said he had lost power at that moment, while DTM chief Gerhard Berger thought the incident was a misjudgement and not deliberate. Berger also named van der Linde as the man of the race, even though the BMW driver lost third place on the last lap and finished fifth.
For R-Motorsport, Dennis’s sixth place was the high point of a weekend that also brought a double retirement on Sunday and di Resta’s non-start. The next round is at Misano on 8–9 June.

facts.v: Rast won in 59:24.539 over 39 laps, with Eng second and Green third, 11.791 seconds behind.
Sheldon van der Linde took his first DTM pole with 1:21.590, 0.006 seconds ahead of Rast.
